title: By the pen
hook: by the pen and what they write (68:1)

segments.voice: Yesterday: ar-Rahman, holding the birds in the air. Your line was held by the merciful. Today a new surah opens with an oath.

When people swear an oath, they swear by something big. By God. By my mother's life. On the Bible, on the Qur'an, on everything I love. Several surahs of the Qur'an open with an oath by grand things: the sun, the dawn, the night, the stars. Then there's surah sixty-eight. It swears by an object you probably have in a drawer, a bag, or behind your ear right now. A pen. And by what people write with it.

Surah al-Qalam, the Pen, verse one, in Pickthall's translation: "Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith)." It starts with a single letter, nun, one of the separate letters that open some surahs. What it means, the Qur'an doesn't say. Some scholars say only Allah knows; early commentators offered guesses, an inkwell, a great fish, and the guesses stayed guesses. Then the oath: wa al-qalam, by the pen. Think about where this was heard. Mecca was a place of memory and speech, where poets recited aloud, and the Qur'an describes the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself as unlettered. And yet the revelation keeps pointing at writing. The verses tradition counts as the first revealed, in surah al-'Alaq, say the Most Generous taught by the pen, taught people what they did not know. Here the pen is something to swear by. A hadith in Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi goes further: the first thing Allah created was the pen, and it was told to write. Scholars discuss what that pen is; it isn't pictured as an ordinary one. But the honor reaches the ordinary one too. A scrawled grocery list, a letter to a grandmother, a page of notes before an exam: all of it belongs to what the verse calls that which they write.
screen: `BY THE PEN, AND WHAT THEY WRITE.`

segments.voice: Find a pen and something to write on; the back of a receipt is fine, and a phone will do if that's all you have. Let one thing you're grateful for rise up, then write it in a single line, slowly, letter by letter, as if the writing mattered. Read it back once.
Al-Qalam. The Pen, opening with the letter nun and an oath by the pen and what people write, from a revelation that says Allah taught by the pen. Today's word.
Your line: even your grocery list counts. The oath takes in every line. That's day six hundred forty.

howItsDone: Muslims hold writing in high honor: the verses tradition counts as the first revealed mention the pen, surah 68 swears by it, and calligraphy, above all of the Qur'an, is a treasured art.

chat.says: Why would the Qur'an swear by something as ordinary as a pen?
options: It honors writing; the oath covers the pen and all that people write.
Because writing was the main way Mecca shared its poetry back then.
Because only scholars' writing counts; everyday writing doesn't.
